v.rationale: All three are functionally equivalent and correct. Each has an identical migration (string(30) nullable after name), the same `present|nullable|string|max:30` FormRequest, a Fillable update, auth:sanctum routes and RefreshDatabase enabled. All suites pass (impl-2: 15, impl-3: 13, impl-1: 17). My probes found no bugs in any of them: 31 multibyte chars rejected, whitespace trimmed to null, integer rejected, real-token PATCH works, form-encoded PATCH works, email not leaked. Idiom and test quality decide the ranking. impl-1 uses an API Resource with `$wrap=null`, so the output is flat as the spec describes, and has the broadest tests (real Sanctum token, multibyte boundary, user isolation, mass-assignment guard). Its weak points are some duplicated tests that a dataset would collapse and key-only validation assertions. impl-2 is equally well built and has the most idiomatic Pest (datasets, message-level assertions). It loses a little for silently wrapping the payload in `data` and for an unnecessary prefix/'/' route group. impl-3 is the leanest, using `tap()` and `only()`, which suits the task's size. But it repeats the response field list instead of using a Resource, and its tests are thinner (no other-user isolation test, and the boundary test doesn't check persistence).
